Now that Mathlib is on v4.28.0-rc1 and the new shake is available as lake shake, it's time to update Mathlib CI so it runs lake shake again. I think the current preferred settings are lake shake --add-public --keep-implied --keep-prefix and --fix is you want it to apply the changes.

Currently this suggests quite a few changes, so we'll have to make another PR before enabling this in CI.

Does anyone know the current state of automatically adding commits to a PR? I would love to not have to run shake myself, and to have CI run it, try rebuilding, and if that worked just apply the changes automatically.
#34511
(@Johan Commelin, I used the x <command line> format for the commit message. Is your machinery ready to handle this?)

@Sebastian Ullrich, something I don't see how to do currently is to only run shake on a single file. I'd like to be able to do this, so it minimizes the imports of just that one file (plus adding imports as required downstream, of course).

I think this would be quite useful when looking at the rebuild critical path e.g. https://speed.lean-lang.org/mathlib4-out/be6dc76a4049aab3ce7ae14bfd2a19720c8f43d2/

(I only just learnt how to find the rebuild critical path today:

  • go to https://radar.lean-lang.org
  • select "mathlib4" in the top right (or jump direct to https://radar.lean-lang.org/repos/mathlib4)
  • select a recent commit (most recent at the top)
  • click "Lakeprof report"
#mathlib4 > The long pole in mathlib @ 💬

Sebastian Ullrich, something I don't see how to do currently is to only run shake on a single file. I'd like to be able to do this, so it minimizes the imports of just that one file (plus adding imports as required downstream, of course).

Can you say more, is it that you want to run this specific file under different flags than the rest?
I don't want any suggestions for anything upstream of it, but I want to convert public import to import just in that file.

Making sure that the base commit has already been shaken is likely the easiest option to avoid unrelated changes, no? Then I think you can just do import changes yourself in the file (which gives you more control on e.g. removing only a subset of public imports) and rerun shake afterwards. As it will use the oleans from the working base commit, it should understand that it needs to add imports to unbreak downstream files, even if the package is not actually buildable before doing so. I'll see if I can test this on Yaël's example

Kim Morrison said:

Does anyone know the current state of automatically adding commits to a PR? I would love to not have to run shake myself, and to have CI run it, try rebuilding, and if that worked just apply the changes automatically.

Mathlib uses pre-commit whose config is in .pre-commit-config.yaml.
Currently it only removes trailing whitespace and then commits automatically, e.g. this commit in #34353.

It seems pretty easy to add hooks from the current repo, just need to add an entry in the config that says to run lake shake --fix ....

(I'm not sure if there are some other ways Mathlib commits automatically. It can be done without pre-commit of course, but it's a nice existing framework that is externally maintained)

I've encountered a weird situation on the shake PR. #34511

At commit c997929cf0568c908e2de8476739b89ce8240ae9 (the current head of that PR branch), lake build Mathlib.Control.Traversable.Equiv produces an error, but opening the file in VSCode it looks fine.

Would someone be able to try reproducing this for me? It is potentially a module system bug.
I can confirm that I get error: Mathlib/Control/Traversable/Equiv.lean:138:29: Unknown identifier `functor_norm` on command line and it builds fine in VS Code.

Hovering over functor_norm in VS Code I get the surprising message

A simp lemma specification is:

  • optional ↑ or ↓ to specify use before or after entering the subterm
  • optional ← to use the lemma backward
  • thm for the theorem to rewrite with
Okay, can I bump this one up to some combination of @Sebastian Ullrich, @Mac Malone and @Marc Huisinga? Divergences between lake build and VS Code triggered by running shake seems tricky.

@Kim Morrison Within the module system, the server loads more data about its imports than lake build does. Namely, it loads server metadata from olean.server and compiled code from .ir (e.g., for #eval to work). If elaboration relies on this additional data, a build can fail where the interactive session does not. For instance, shake may have removed a meta import in the transitive import graph that some Mathlib meta code (e.g., for prodoucing functor_norm) needed but Shake thought was unnecessary.
Sadly, I am not sufficiently familiar with the breadth of Mathlib meta code to likely be able to debug this.

FWIW adding import Mathlib.Tactic.Attr.Register (the file where docs#Parser.Attr.functor_norm is defined) (or adding public import Mathlib.Tactic.Attr.Register) to Mathlib/Control/Traversable/Equiv.lean makes this file build on command line.

Okay, this took a short while to analyze in full depth. The issue indeed is that functor_norm simply isn't imported anymore, so the cmdline behavior is correct; lean#12375 will ensure shake does not discard such imports. The divergence between server and cmdline here is a separate issue, which ultimately stems from simpsets being registered via initialize. This part will require some more thinking.

I've started working on a run of lake shake --fix on mathlib4 in #37807. The first thing that jumps out at me is all of the additions of meta import Mathlib.Tactic.Attr.Register. I guess we could get these to go away by adding a public import somewhere low in the import hierarchy, but this would undo #32541 by @Yaël Dillies which made it private. I'm guessing something has changed in shake since the last successful full run in #34511?

I'm still getting up to speed on shake so I don't know enough to know what we should do here -- any guidance would be welcome!
It's okay if you undo my PR, it was experimental

I took a look at why the import in Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Subalgebra.Rank appeared: it is because the file uses the nontriviality tactic which at some point runs simp [nontriviality, ...] and @[nontriviality] is defined in Attr.Register. Now usually this is just how tactic programming works: you have to think not only about the imports that make your tactic elaborate but also the ones that allow your tactic to run successfully in other modules, which you should add as public imports of your tactic. It is only through an implementation detail of simp attributes that you are allowed to refer to them without actually having the module in question imported (directly or via transitive public imports), like you would have to with most other named references in Lean. Shake does not know about this edge case and my recommendation would be not to rely on it in the implementation of nontriviality either, by declaring such a public import:

--- a/Mathlib/Tactic/Nontriviality/Core.lean
+++ b/Mathlib/Tactic/Nontriviality/Core.lean
@@ -7,6 +7,7 @@ module

 public meta import Qq.MetaM
 public import Mathlib.Logic.Nontrivial.Basic -- shake: keep (tactic dependency)
+public import Mathlib.Tactic.Attr.Register -- shake: keep (tactic dependency)
 public meta import Mathlib.Tactic.ToDual

Note the other shake-kept import that already exists for the reason I mentioned.

This does additionally make sure that the modules being able to access the nontriviality tactic also can use the @[nontriviality] attribute without further imports, which only seems consistent to me.
I haven't checked yet whether that would get rid of all the new imports or whether there are similar cases in other metaprograms

I should also mention that I've considered a change to Shake that would make it discard new imports it thinks are necessary but that evidently were not necessary to elaborate the current state of the module, which would be the case here. My fear was that this could obscure Shake bugs we want to fix though this is a first case where it would improve Shake's output while not being related to a clear bug in Shake.
Thanks! To make sure I understand what qualifies as a bug: if shake --fix makes a change to imports and afterwards mathlib does not compile, that should be minimized and reported, right?

Definitely, yes! Problems in the other direction like above are report-worthy as well, it just turns out in this specific case that likely Lean rather than Shake should be changed, but in a nontrivial way for not much benefit outside of Shake

Just curious: I notice that the effects of any initializer seem to ignore import visibility barriers, and so we e.g. propagate linters and can use attributes even when not properly imported (and you can tell the attribute is not properly imported by the docstring not appearing on hover for @[foo] :) ).

Is this the way you mean lean (maybe) should be changed? And is it good practice to design import hierarchies "expecting" that initializers are just going to disregard visibility, or should we "pretend" they respect it, so to speak? :) (For attributes it seems to make sense to want them publicly imported to preserve hovers; for things like linters it maybe is useful that they see through visibility barriers!)

We cannot restrict further what initializers are run as metaprogramming code downstream may depend on them. We can only ensure on a case-by-case level that their side effects affect elaboration in well-scoped ways, by changing how the data they generated is being used. This may include moving some concepts like custom attributes away from being based on initializers in the first place.

I'm unclear what's going on here. My understanding is that shake used to run automatically but no longer does, and our imports aren't well minimised any more? Does #min_imports work with the module system? I was moving stuff to a new file just now and #min_imports found a -50 imports that had just been sitting there.

Yes, that's more or less the case. I'm in the process of minimizing some bugs in shake; after those are reported, I'll clean up a PR with "good" suggestions from shake and then we can add it to our CI again.
